title: Endometriosis on TikTok: Evaluating social media misinformation and the role of healthcare professionals
screen_reason: Cross-sectional content analysis of the top 100 TikTok videos under each of three endometriosis search terms (298 analysed). Videos were judged against current clinical knowledge with ACOG guidelines as the reference and the paper reports the share containing incorrect or misleading information (69/298 = 23.2%), plus per-category shares. That is a CONTENT prevalence estimate with an external ground truth and a stated denominator.

estimates.country: United States (videos searched from a new account through a VPN service with a United States server; non-English videos excluded)
estimates.measure_type: % of top endometriosis TikTok videos containing incorrect or misleading information about causes, treatment, symptoms or other aspects of endometriosis
estimates.denominator: 298 TikTok videos analysed: the top 100 valid videos under each of the three most popular endometriosis search terms ('Endometriosis', 'Endometriosis in teens', 'Endometriosis remedies'); 331 screened, 300 analysed, 2 later excluded
estimates.definition: Video contained incorrect or misleading information in at least one of four categories adapted from Acero et al. 2023: incorrect causes, incorrect symptoms, incorrect treatment, other incorrect information (a video with several types is counted once here)
estimates.misinfo_def: No formal definition; operationalised as content contradicting 'current clinical knowledge with the ACOG guidelines as the main resource', including causes 'either incorrect or not clinically validated' and treatments 'that have not been clinically validated'
estimates.source_quote: Overall, out of 298 videos, 69 videos (23.2%) had
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Factual content assessed by a single reviewer (SI) against current clinical knowledge with the ACOG guidelines as the main resource; a second reviewer (EH) was consulted only when factualness or category was unclear, to reach consensus. Stability check: the same reviewer re-analysed 50% of videos (150) and 5 (3.0%) were re-coded. The authors explicitly note the data were NOT scored by a second independent rater and repeatability/rater bias were not examined.
estimates.moderator_quote: This study examined the top 100 videos under three popular endometriosis search terms; "Endometriosis," "Endometriosis in teens," and "Endometriosis remedies," which were determined by TikTok's autocomplete predictions ... The top videos were searched using a new account through a VPN service with a United States server. Non-English, inaudible, duplicated, or irrelevant (i.e. not related to endometriosis) videos were excluded from analysis, with the next video in sequence taking its place.
estimates.notes: Denominator is every video in the topical sample (items that exist as surfaced by search) -> CONTENT. denom_selection=curated because the frame is the top-100 algorithmically ranked results per search term. country_norm=United States reflects the sampling locale (US VPN, English-only); the creators' own countries are never reported, so an adjudicator could alternatively read this as Global - flagged here rather than in borderline because the sampling decision is explicit. breadth=misleading because the numerator includes 'not clinically validated' causes and treatments, not only demonstrably false claims. 23.2% is the verbatim Results value; the abstract rounds it to 23%.  QUOTE NOTE: the v2 text extraction interleaves the article's columns, so no longer contiguous span of the published sentence is recoverable; source_quote is the exact contiguous span carrying the value, and the full published sentence is: "Overall, out of 298 videos, 69 videos (23.2%) had incorrect or misleading information about causes, treatment, symptoms, or information about endometriosis (Table 3)." (Results, p. 6); the abstract states the same as "Overall, out of 298 videos, 69 videos (23%) had incorrect or misleading information about causes, treatment, symptoms, or information about endometriosis."

estimates.measure_type: % of top endometriosis TikTok videos presenting clinically unvalidated treatments/cures (treatment misinformation)
estimates.denominator: 298 TikTok videos analysed (top 100 valid videos under each of three endometriosis search terms)
estimates.definition: Video presented information on treatments and cures for endometriosis that have not been clinically validated, including herbal remedies, acupuncture, juice cleanses, anti-inflammatory diets or supplements

estimates.source_quote: (14.1%) presented information on treatments and cures
estimates.page_loc: Results, p. 6; repeated in Discussion ('significantly high amounts of misinformation about treatment (14.1%)')
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Same single-rater protocol with consensus adjudication by a second reviewer where unclear; 3.0% re-code rate on a 150-video stability check.
estimates.moderator_quote: Forty-two videos (14.1%) presented information on treatments and cures for endometriosis that have not been clinically validated ... The most common type of misinformation pertained to endometriosis treatment.
estimates.notes: ADJUDICATOR: this is a SUBSET of the 69 videos in the main row (a single misinformation category), recorded because the paper makes it a headline in the Discussion. definition_variant=true; must NOT be pooled alongside the 23.2% row. The other three categories (incorrect causes 21 = 7.0%, incorrect symptoms 4 = 1.3%, other incorrect information 15) are listed in missed_or_uncertain rather than given rows, per R4.  QUOTE NOTE: the v2 text extraction interleaves the article's columns, so no longer contiguous span of the published sentence is recoverable; source_quote is the exact contiguous span carrying the value, and the full published sentence is: "Forty-two videos (14.1%) presented information on treatments and cures for endometriosis that have not been clinically validated, including herbal remedies, acupuncture, juice cleanses, anti-inflammatory diets, or supplements." (Results, p. 6).

missed_or_uncertain: (1) The three remaining misinformation categories are reported with the same 298 denominator: incorrect causes 21 videos (7.0%), incorrect symptoms 4 videos (1.3%), other incorrect information 15 videos (percentage not stated; 15/298 = 5.0% would be derivable). They are category subsets of the 69-video main row, so only the largest (treatments) is given a variant row, per R4 (quality over quantity) and to avoid double counting. (2) Table 3 also splits the categories by search term (e.g. 37 of the 42 incorrect-treatment videos came from 'Endometriosis remedies') and Table 5 splits misinformation videos by source type and attitude (physician 2 vs non-physician 53 with positive/neutral attitudes). These are sub-group breakdowns of the same sample, not distinct country/platform/measure cells, and the physician/non-physician contrast is reported only as p-values without shares of the respective denominators (50 physician vs 248 non-physician videos), so no subgroup rows are extracted. (3) Attitude coding (Table 4: 181 positive/neutral, 101 negative, 16 mixed) is not a veracity judgement, so no row. (4) 'Only 1% of the analyzed videos discussed medication management other than COCPs' and 'only three of the 298 reviewed videos discussed clinically validated, non-surgical treatments' are coverage/omission measures, not falsity shares - closer to QUALITY and not extracted. (5) '67% of patients with endometriosis used social media to gather information ... and 92% reported that they learned new information' is cited from another study (ref 3) and is excluded by R8. (6) View, share and comment counts (139,680,532 total views) are engagement descriptives with no misinformation denominator, so no exposure, reach or concentration row is possible.

rob.design: Cross-sectional content analysis, single day (16 June 2023). Frame: TikTok's top results for three autocomplete-derived search terms, viewed from a fresh account via a US VPN; non-English, inaudible, duplicate and irrelevant videos replaced by the next video in sequence until 100 valid videos per term (331 screened, 300 analysed, 2 later excluded, 298 final). Metadata pulled with an open-source TikTok API tool. Coding: one primary reviewer (SI) against ACOG guidelines, second reviewer (EH) consulted for unclear cases; four misinformation categories adapted from Acero et al. 2023, multiple categories per video allowed. Reliability: stability re-code of 150 videos by the SAME rater, 5/150 (3.0%) re-coded; no independent second rater - the authors state this limits identification of rater bias. Other limitations acknowledged: algorithmic personalisation despite the neutral account, single-day snapshot. No IRB required (public data, no human subjects).
rob.item6_quote: Erroneous information about endometriosis was sorted into four types adapted from Acero et al, 2023: incorrect information about causes of endometriosis, incorrect information about endometriosis symptoms, incorrect information about endometriosis treatment, and other incorrect information about endometriosis.
rob.item10_quote: Overall, out of 298 videos, 69 videos (23.2%) had incorrect or misleading information about causes, treatment, symptoms, or information about endometriosis (Table 3).
